manifest.notes: SqueekMatchEscrow is the fee-free SqueekMatch market on Sepolia. Constructor arguments are the existing SqueekNFT and SqueekToken (SQK), respectively, matching the accepted source's deployment constants (script/DeploySqueekMatchEscrow.s.sol, README deployment table) and https://docs.squeekchain.com/assets/deployments/sepolia.json. It has no owner, admin or proxy and needs no initialization or deployment ETH; the constructor makes no external call. SqueekMining and SqueekCore are resolved through SqueekNFT at use. Asks and swaps keep NFTs in their holders' wallets until fill; bids and maker-funded swaps escrow SQK. Orders default to 7 days and allow at most 30 days. Cancelling an expired bid or swap refunds escrowed SQK to its maker. On-chain check, 2026-11-02, public Sepolia RPC: the NFT argument returns name Squeek, symbol SQUEEK and mining() = 0x3beE588fC20dE788Bac17d33b41Da7346cb27EC4; that SqueekMining's configuration() names this same SQK token and this same NFT and core() = 0x74665DaEca35A2303e767e76a2fF1fB6f93E119f; collectionPolicy(0) names the NFT with maximum level 10; the SQK argument returns symbol SQK and 18 decimals. Review finding, 2026-11-02: https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/economy/state reports token 0x5501e1fa81be1c3f49225fa7668da0245d07db60 and a different core/mining graph from the documented deployment and accepted constants. That address also has code and also reports symbol SQK, so a symbol check cannot tell the two apart; only an address comparison can. This manifest preserves the accepted deployment inputs. Resolve the deployment-identity conflict before enabling trading; the approved brief requires refusing trading on mismatch.
